title: `LookupCellRenderer` answers one epistemic state two opposite ways: a name-shaped unresolvable reference prints as a confident name, an opaque-shaped one loses its raw value to a muted dash
body:
Found while implementing objectui#8434, which repaired exactly this class for `user`. Filed rather than fixed there: that card's subject is `UserCellRenderer`, and this is a second renderer with its own already-shipped affordance and its own trade-off.

## Measured, on `da5e4f69e`, in the same mounted tree as objectui#8434's readings

`getCellRenderer('lookup')` with `reference_to: 'sys_user'`:

| value | rendered |
|---|---|
| `'Ada Lovelace'` (a name written into a reference column) | `span class="block max-w-full truncate" title="Ada Lovelace"` containing `Ada Lovelace` — **unmuted, no marker** |
| `'01HQZX9K2M4N6P8R'` (opaque, unresolvable) | `span class="block max-w-full truncate text-muted-foreground" title="—"` containing `—` |

So `LookupCellRenderer` splits the SAME epistemic state — a reference this screen did not resolve — into two visually opposite answers, and the split is decided by `isLikelyOpaqueId`, i.e. by **the shape of the string**, not by whether anything resolved.

## Two problems, opposite in direction

**1. A name-shaped unresolvable value is presented as a resolved name.** This is objectui#8434's defect verbatim, one renderer over. `resolveLabel`'s last arm is `return { text: String(val), muted: false }` — an unresolved reference rendered as ordinary, confident text. Nothing says the reference is invalid. A dirty `lookup` row therefore reads exactly like a clean one.

**2. An opaque-shaped unresolvable value has its raw value destroyed.** The muted `—` replaces the id entirely. objectui#8434's triage note names why that is a cost, in the context of the strong arm it argued against: the raw string *"is the only clue for diagnosing existing dirty rows"*. Here the value is gone from the cell text; only the `title` carries `"—"`, not the id. `ReferencedRecordLink` still wraps it, so the id survives in the href — but nothing readable shows it.

## What objectui#8434 settled that applies here

- The affordance should be **additive** (a stated marker), because absence of a name is a subtractive signal and a subtractive signal is not a signal.
- The sentence must be **epistemic** ("this screen did not resolve it"), never ontological ("not found"), because an unexpanded id is the legitimate stored form and the renderer cannot tell it from dirty data.
- The raw value should stay **visible**, since it is the only diagnostic for an existing bad row.

`packages/fields/src/index.tsx` now has `UnresolvedUserReference` doing exactly that for `user`. Whether `lookup` should share it is the decision this card is for — it is a bigger surface than `user` (`lookup` / `master_detail` / `tree` all route through `LookupCellRenderer`), it has a fetch-on-demand resolver `user` does not (`useLookupName`), so it can genuinely distinguish "fetched and absent" from "never fetched", and its `—` is already-shipped behaviour that people may rely on.

⛔ Not a request to loosen anything on the save path. Display only, same as objectui#8434.
